messages:
support_sara: Heads up — ACME is seeing intermittent 401s + embedding latency spikes since ~2026-03-17 14:20 UTC. Two representative request ids from their side: r-20260317-1a2b3c and r-20260317-1a2b3d. Attaching short timeline in next message. Need minimal repro snippets (curl / py / js / go) and clear debug-bundle instructions we can send to customer. Priority P1.

customer_success_maya: Timeline from customer: 14:20:10 first spike, 14:21:03 got a 401, then ~14:23 a few timeouts. They said token rotation is automatic on their side. Will ask them to run commands and share output.

eng-ml_john: Thanks. First ask them to run a single curl that preserves response headers so we can capture the x-request-id and auth failure details. Quick curl to send them:

```bash
curl -v -sS 
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" 
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" 
  -H "X-Request-ID: my-local-$(date +%s)" 
  --data '{"model":"embedding-001","input":"test latency probe"}' 
  https://api.redwood.example/v1/embeddings
```

Tell them to paste both the response headers and the full body. If they get 401 include the header block (the -v output) so we can see WWW-Authenticate, Date, and x-request-id.

eng-runtime_lee: Also ask them to run with --dump-header out.txt so they can attach the exact headers file. If they can run the curl twice (one that fails, one that succeeds) keep both header dumps; we need both request ids to correlate traces. If customer is OK, capture SDK logs at DEBUG (env var REDWOOD_LOG=debug) and upload as part of the debug bundle.

support_sara: Minimal Python repro they can run quickly (no deps except requests):

```python
# save as repro_embed.py
import requests, os
url = 'https://api.redwood.example/v1/embeddings'
token = os.getenv('TOKEN')
headers = {'Authorization': f'Bearer {token}', 'Content-Type': 'application/json', 'X-Request-ID': 'py-' + str(int(__import__('time').time()))}
resp = requests.post(url, json={'model':'embedding-001','input':'probe'}, headers=headers)
print('STATUS', resp.status_code)
print('HEADERS', resp.headers)
print('BODY', resp.text)
```

Have them run: TOKEN=<their-token> python repro_embed.py and paste stdout.

customer_success_maya: Customer ran the curl, got a 401 and attached header dump (pasted here):

"HTTP/1.1 401 Unauthorized
x-request-id: r-20260317-1a2b3c
content-type: application/json; charset=utf-8
date: Wed, 17 Mar 2026 14:21:04 GMT
content-length: 92

{\"error\":\"authentication failed: token expired\"}"

They also ran the python repro twice — first run 200, second run 401 within ~45s. Will share both outputs.

devex_ana: Quick JS (node-fetch) snippet they can run to toggle token header and capture IDs:

```javascript
// repro.js
const fetch = require('node-fetch');
(async () => {
  const token = process.env.TOKEN;
  const res = await fetch('https://api.redwood.example/v1/embeddings', {
    method: 'POST',
    headers: {
      'Authorization': `Bearer ${token}`,
      'Content-Type': 'application/json',
      'X-Request-ID': 'js-' + Date.now()
    },
    body: JSON.stringify({model: 'embedding-001', input: 'probe'})
  });
  console.log('STATUS', res.status);
  console.log('HEADERS', Object.fromEntries(res.headers));
  console.log('BODY', await res.text());
})();
```

eng-ml_john: And a minimal Go example (single file) for their infra team:

```go
// go-repro.go
package main
import (
  "bytes"
  "fmt"
  "io/ioutil"
  "net/http"
  "os"
)
func main(){
  token := os.Getenv("TOKEN")
  req, _ := http.NewRequest("POST", "https://api.redwood.example/v1/embeddings", bytes.NewBufferString(`{"model":"embedding-001","input":"probe"}`))
  req.Header.Set("Authorization", "Bearer "+token)
  req.Header.Set("Content-Type", "application/json")
  req.Header.Set("X-Request-ID", "go-"+fmt.Sprint(timeNow()))
  resp, err := http.DefaultClient.Do(req)
  if err!=nil{ fmt.Println("ERR", err); return }
  b, _ := ioutil.ReadAll(resp.Body)
  fmt.Println("STATUS", resp.StatusCode)
  fmt.Println("HEADERS", resp.Header)
  fmt.Println("BODY", string(b))
}
// helper omitted: timeNow -> use time.Now().Unix() when running
```

eng-runtime_lee: For the debug bundle instruct them to: 1) collect SDK logs (DEBUG) 2) attach the curl header dump files for failing and succeeding calls 3) include environment: SDK versions, region, whether behind a proxy/load balancer, and token rotation config 4) include the two request ids (r-20260317-1a2b3c and r-20260317-1a2b3d). Use our secure upload link: https://upload.redwood.example/debug-bundle (customer must paste the upload id here).

customer_success_maya: Uploaded the header dumps and python outputs to the temp upload id UPL-9f8e7d. Also included SDK version python-redwood==0.4.3 and that they're running via an internal auth proxy which rotates tokens every 60s.

eng-ml_john: Perfect — we need both request ids. We'll pull traces once the upload is available. If the customer can run the curl with the extra header `X-Debug: 1` we return extended internal debug headers (use only for support). Ask them to include that run too.

support_sara: I'll message the customer with the four snippets and step-by-step instructions (curl with --dump-header, python, node, go, env vars to set, ask for X-Debug run). Will attach upload id and ask them to keep both raw header files. Thanks everyone — I’ll update the ticket when we have the trace correlation. :thumbsup:
